record.title: Revised Hessian tail inequality and even-mixture equality
record.locator: Lemma 2.9, equation (2.8), and Remark 2.10; the long record supplies its own zero-field endpoint proof.

aligned_passages.text: **A coefficient budget from the first curvature moment.** Full support also bounds the minimizing coefficient. Put $m(t)=\mathbb E a(t,X_t)$. The compact-strip identity $$ da(t,X_t)=-\gamma(t)a(t,X_t)^2\,dt+b(t,X_t)\,dB_t $$ holds before any smoothness conclusion for $\gamma$; the bounded strip derivatives make its stochastic integral a martingale. [OpenAI (2026a), proof of Corollary 6.4][fs-density]. At zero, $X_0=0$, $a(0,0)\ge0$ and $\mathbb E a(0,X_0)^2=1$ give $a(0,0)=1$. Taking expectations and using $\mathbb E a(t,X_t)^2=1$ therefore yields $$ m(t)=1-\int_0^t\gamma(s)\,ds,\qquad 0\le t<1. $$ Convexity gives $m(t)\ge0$. Letting $t\uparrow1$ and using monotonicity of $\gamma$ on every tail gives $$ \int_0^1\gamma(s)\,ds\le1,\qquad 0\le\gamma(t)\le\frac{m(t)}{1-t}\le\frac1{1-t}. $$ Indeed, $(s-t)\gamma(t)\le\int_t^s\gamma\le m(t)$ for $t **Proposition 6.2 (terminal normalization in zero field).** For the minimizer and diffusion of Theorem 5.1, $$ \lim_{t\uparrow1}m(t)=0,\qquad \int_0^1\gamma(s)\,ds=1,\qquad m(t)=\int_t^1\gamma(s)\,ds, $$ and consequently $$ P_*=\int_0^1s\gamma(s)\,ds. $$ Thus $\gamma(s)\,ds$ has total mass one; this does not normalize the Stieltjes measure $d\gamma$. This is an ordinary analytic consequence, separate from the selected formal endpoints. **Proof.** The backward comparison in §4.3 gives $\Phi_{xxx}(t,x)\le0$ for $x>0$ in every positive finite-step approximation. Compact-strip convergence of the third spatial derivative passes this inequality to $\gamma$. Together with evenness and convexity, it says that $a(t,x)$ is nonnegative, even and nonincreasing in $|x|$. These inputs are [OpenAI (2026a), Lemma 3.2][fs-signs] and [Lemma 2.1][fs-reg]; they do not require differentiability of $\gamma$. Uniform terminal convergence to $|x|$ and convex difference quotients give $u(t,x)\to1$ at every fixed $x>0$. For each $\delta>0$, $$ 0\le a(t,\delta) \le\frac2\delta\int_{\delta/2}^{\delta}a(t,x)\,dx =\frac2\delta\bigl(u(t,\delta)-u(t,\delta/2)\bigr) \longrightarrow0. $$ The spatial monotonicity is essential here: convergence of convex functions alone would not imply convergence of their second derivatives. It remains to control the probability of the shrinking region where curvature can be large. Oddness and monotonicity give $u(t,x)\ge0$ for $x\ge0$, so the drift points away from zero. Tanaka's formula for $R_t=|X_t|$ gives $$ R_t=W_t+V_t+L_t,\qquad W_t=\int_0^t\operatorname{sgn}(X_s)\,dB_s,\qquad V_t=\int_0^t\gamma(s)u(s,R_s)\,ds. $$ Here $L$ is the local time of $X$ at zero. The occupation-time formula and $d\langle X\rangle_s=ds$ imply $\int_0^t\mathbf1_{\{X_s=0\}}\,ds=0$. Thus $\langle W\rangle_t=t$, and the continuous martingale $W$ is Brownian motion. The process $V$ is nondecreasing and starts at zero; $L$ increases only when $R=0$. The reflection formula therefore gives, pathwise, $$ R_t=W_t+V_t-\min\left(0,\inf_{s\le t}(W_s+V_s)\right) \ge W_t-\min\left(0,\inf_{s\le t}W_s\right)=:R_t^0. $$ Indeed $0\le V_s\le V_t$ bounds the subtracted minimum by $\min(0,\inf_{s\le t}W_s)+V_t$. No independence of $V$ and $W$ is needed. Reflected Brownian motion $R_t^0$ has the one-time law $|B_t|$, so for $t>0$, $$ \Pr(|X_t|\le\delta) \le\Pr(|B_t|\le\delta) \le\sqrt{\frac2\pi}\frac{\delta}{\sqrt t}. $$ Splitting at $|X_t|=\delta$, using spatial monotonicity outside and Cauchy–Schwarz with $\mathbb E a(t,X_t)^2=1$ inside, yields $$ 0\le m(t)\le a(t,\delta) +\sqrt{\Pr(|X_t|\le\delta)}. $$ First let $t\uparrow1$ and then $\delta\downarrow0$. This proves $m(1-)=0$. The compact-strip identity for $m$ now gives total mass one and the tail formula. Tonelli and (6.1) give the stated expression for $P_*$. In particular, $$ 0\le P_*-I(T)=\int_T^1(s-T)\gamma(s)\,ds \le(1-T)m(T)=o(1-T). $$ No numerical rate for $m(T)\to0$ or for the required spatial derivative bounds follows from this proof. The endpoint distinction also matters when comparing editions. [Sellke, arXiv:2105.03506v4, Lemma 2.9, equation (2.7)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.03506v4) states the expected-Hessian tail equality. In [version 6, Lemma 2.9, equation (2.8), and Remark 2.10](https://arxiv.org/html/2105.03506v6#S2.SS3), the general statement is an inequality; the remark obtains equality indirectly for even mixtures. The specialized zero-field proof above supplies its own endpoint argument from the shape and contact identities, rather than substituting $t=1$ into a compact-strip formula or relying on the older equality in its full stated generality.
